rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the priority is to establish a simple, low-cost reference point before testing more complex profile, encoder, or fusion choices. config_001 is the minimal RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline, so it isolates basic RNA representation without aggregation or multimodal fusion. Its result will calibrate later comparisons: if it performs well, it becomes a strong anchor for testing learned RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image modality, and fusion; if it underperforms, it motivates shifting budget toward image-only or multimodal configurations. This is the best first experiment because it reduces uncertainty with minimal confounds and avoids prematurely committing to a more complex design.

The only completed experiment is sparse evidence: config_001, an RNA-only single-profile PCA model, achieves moderate validation accuracy (0.485) and F1 (0.464), leaving it unclear whether the single-profile setting is limiting or whether multiple profiles with simple aggregation can improve performance. config_002 keeps the model setting and RNA encoder fixed while testing the minimal multiprofile extension with avgpool, isolating the effect of profile setting and the necessary aggregation choice without introducing new encoders, image data, or fusion. This is the best next experiment under a limited budget because it reduces uncertainty about a key design decision and creates a clean baseline for later comparing transformer aggregation, alternative RNA encoders, or multimodal fusion.

RNA multiprofile with avgpool (config_002) improved validation accuracy and F1 over singleprofile PCA (config_001), suggesting multiprofile aggregation is promising, but it is unclear whether transformer aggregation is better than avgpool. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and pca_n2000 fixed, directly isolating the aggregation effect. Under the limited budget, this is a logical exploitation of the current best setting and will clarify whether added aggregation complexity is worthwhile before testing other encoders or multimodal fusion.

The completed experiments show that RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA is the strongest setting so far, with both higher accuracy and F1 than single-profile PCA or transformer aggregation. The image modality is still untested, so it is unclear whether images provide independent predictive signal or whether a multimodal model would be justified. config_011 tests an image-only baseline using the same multiprofile/avgpool structure as the best RNA experiment but with ResNet-50, isolating the image representation while holding profile and aggregation fixed. This is the best next experiment because it establishes the needed unimodal baseline for later interpreting multimodal fusion results and avoids confounding image usefulness with fusion before testing more complex multimodal configurations.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool, which outperforms singleprofile PCA and multiprofile transformer PCA in both accuracy and F1. The main uncertainty is whether PCA is an optimal RNA representation in this promising setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, so it cleanly tests whether a learned nonlinear RNA representation improves over PCA. This is a good use of the next experiment because it exploits the current best direction while reducing uncertainty about representation quality before adding more complex multimodal fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile avgpool is much stronger than image-only resnet, and scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool is the best completed configuration (accuracy 0.650, F1 0.628). The key remaining uncertainty in the unimodal RNA direction is whether the scgpt encoder can match or exceed scvi_n200 under the same profile and aggregation. config_008 tests only the RNA encoder while holding multiprofile and avgpool fixed, giving a clean comparison to config_005 and config_002. This is the best next use of budget because it either identifies a better representation or confirms scvi_n200, reducing uncertainty before investing in aggregation or multimodal fusion experiments.

RNA-only multiprofile avgpool is currently best, with scvi_n200 outperforming PCA and scGPT (0.650 vs 0.591/0.530 accuracy), and multiprofile helped PCA over singleprofile. The key uncertainty is whether scvi_n200 also requires multiprofile/aggregation or can perform well in a simpler singleprofile setting. config_004 tests scvi_n200 with singleprofile, isolating the profile effect for the best RNA encoder and comparing it to config_001 (singleprofile PCA) and config_005 (multiprofile scvi). This completes the central RNA encoder/profile factorial, avoids adding image/fusion changes, and is likely to clarify whether to keep a simpler singleprofile model before spending budget on more complex multimodal designs.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool (config_005, 0.6501 acc / 0.6275 F1), and for PCA multiprofile avgpool also outperformed transformer (config_002 vs config_003). This leaves uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation could improve the best scvi representation. config_006 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the promising scvi_n200 multiprofile setting, so it directly isolates the aggregation effect. Under a limited budget, this is a low-risk, high-information extension of the current best direction before moving to more complex multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence is RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile (config_005/006, ~0.65), while image-only ResNet50 is weak (config_011, 0.33). The key uncertainty is whether adding image features to the strong RNA model improves validation accuracy or adds noise. config_030 keeps the already-tested strong RNA setting (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) and the already-tested image setting (ResNet50, multiprofile, avgpool), introducing only concat fusion. This allows direct comparison with config_005 and config_011, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion before varying fusion type, aggregation, or image encoder, making it the most informative next step under a limited budget.

The strongest RNA-only models use scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool/transformer, reaching about 0.65 accuracy and 0.63 F1, while the only tested multimodal model (config_030: scvi_n200, multiprofile, ResNet, avgpool, concat) is slightly lower at 0.6315 accuracy and 0.6068 F1. Image-only ResNet is also weak, so it is unclear whether concat fusion is the bottleneck or whether the image branch is simply not helpful. config_031 changes only fusion to weighted while keeping the exact same RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation as config_030, so it cleanly isolates the effect of fusion. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal one-factor extension of the most informative multimodal result, directly tests whether adaptive fusion can make multimodal modeling competitive with the strong RNA-only baseline, and avoids changing multiple design choices at once.
